title: Commissioners' Meeting 04/13/26
tldr: The Board approved a consent agenda that included proclamations (Halifax Resolves 250th anniversary, National Library Week, Public Service Recognition Week, Clerks' Week and National Day of Prayer), a resolution adding Mars Hill and Marshall to the Asheville Regional Housing Consortium, donation of a surplus inflatable slide to Young Life, free transit rides on May 21, and a Sheriff's Office out-of-state training trip. The Board voted unanimously to join Cohort 8 of the Lead for North Carolina fellowship, with a $10,000 county contribution. Commissioners heard the Transylvania Economic Alliance quarterly report and a Hurricane Helene recovery update covering FEMA debris reviews, a USDA block grant for producers and a $40 million Renew NC commercial revitalization program.

keyVotes.description: Approve the consent agenda, including five proclamations, the housing consortium resolution, a surplus slide donation, free transit day and an out-of-state travel request
keyVotes.background: The consent agenda included the March 9, 2026 minutes; Proclamations #16-2026 (250th anniversary of the Halifax Resolves), #14-2026 (National Library Week), #13-2026 (National Public Service Recognition Week), #17-2026 (Clerks to the Boards of County Commissioners' Week) and #18-2026 (National Day of Prayer); and Resolution #15-2026 authorizing an amended Joint Cooperation Agreement adding Mars Hill and Marshall to the Asheville Regional Housing Consortium. It also included Resolution #12-2026 donating a surplus inflatable slide to Young Life Transylvania County at no cost, permission for the Transportation Department to provide free transit on May 21, 2026 for Strive Not to Drive Week, and approval for a Sheriff's Office officer to attend a one-day search and seizure training in South Carolina on April 14, 2026, funded in the department's budget.

keyVotes.description: Join Cohort 8 of the Lead for North Carolina fellowship and allocate $10,000 as the County's share
keyVotes.background: Lead for North Carolina offered the County an 11-month, full-time paid fellow beginning in late summer 2026, who would preliminarily be assigned to the Clerk to the Board to help with incomplete projects and administrative workflow. The total cost per fellow is about $64,000, but the County's contribution was reduced to $10,000 through UNC School of Government grant support, with the program covering other personnel costs including benefits.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioners discussed program logistics and past experience with similar fellowships. The County Manager noted that housing and salary arrangements are handled through the fellowship program.

keyVotes.background: Motion to adjourn after all business was concluded.

topics.text: Requested that the Rural Development Authority give a future presentation to the Board.
Asked about the status of waterway debris removal; staff said these cases remain under FEMA review.
Spoke about attending the funeral of the late Representative Mike Clampitt and recognized his legacy as a firefighter and public servant.
Thanked fellow Commissioners for supporting his effort to be considered for appointment to the vacant legislative seat, noting the outcome was decided by a single vote.
Addressed public misconceptions about the former Ecusta property, noting continued development potential at the site.
Clarified that the Rural Development Authority is not a county department but an independent entity created by special legislation of the General Assembly with its own funding structure.
Referenced increased long-term wildfire risk from storm debris in forested areas.
Emphasized the existing burn ban and the importance of continued caution to prevent wildfires.
Congratulated Ms. Ferguson on her appointment to the vacant legislative seat and thanked Commissioner Chapman for his continued service and advocacy.

publicComments.speaker: Jonathan Rich
publicComments.summary: Introduced his Lightning Media company and its local news website, The Brevard Beagle.

publicComments.speaker: Doug Powell
publicComments.summary: Spoke about the anniversary of the Halifax Resolves and recent commemorative events held in Halifax, North Carolina.

followUps.description: Arrange a future presentation to the Board on the Rural Development Authority, as requested by Commissioner Chapman.
followUps.resolution: In TEA's annual report, Burton Hodges updated the Board on the Rural Development Authority, including transfer of its administration to the Land of Sky Regional Council and its focus on the former Ecusta property.
